Thanks @bdraco! I want to stop execution and avoid calling `async_add_entities` if a KeyError is encountered - is there a way to do this without having all the code inside the `try`?
@lawtancool instead of calling `async_add_entities` many times, create a list and add it all at the end of the loop. Once you detect a key error, skip the rest of the loop by calling `continue`

So does Home Assistant allow you to turn on/off and **change the brightness** of those lights?
Yes. I configured two light cards to control the dimmers.

For those who are curious, the original issue was caused because Control4 doesn't provide info on whether a light can be dimmed if it is not a Control4-brand wireless wall light switch. 

The fix just enables dimming functionality by default if the integration cannot tell if it is available or not.
